test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Kisna buys a cow for ₹15,000. After one year, he sells it for ₹18,500. After one year, again he buys the same cow at ₹19,000 and sells it for ₹22,300. What is the overall profit percentage of Kisna?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost Price (CP) = 15,000 + 19,000 = 34,000

Total Selling Price (SP) = 18,500 + 22,300 = 40,800

Total Profit = 40,800 − 34,000 = 6,800

Profit% = (6,800 ÷ 34,000) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First CP = 15,000, First SP = 18,500; Second CP = 19,000, Second SP = 22,300.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/921763d5e9a3a4e65b464c9b7d81d36a4c96c7a285d8112000df1d4bd41654c9.png] 

⇒ **Profit 1** = 18,500 − 15,000 = 3,500

⇒ **Profit 2** = 22,300 − 19,000 = 3,300

⇒ **Total Profit** = 3,500 + 3,300 = 6,800

⇒ **Total CP** = 15,000 + 19,000 = 34,000

⇒ **Profit%** = (6,800 ÷ 34,000) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overall Profit Calculation

When multiple transactions occur for the same or different items, the **overall profit percentage** is calculated by dividing the sum of individual profits by the sum of individual cost prices.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when **Selling Price (SP)** is greater than **Cost Price (CP)**. Loss occurs when CP is greater than SP.</p
